evidence.text: George attended our outpatient service. He has an established diagnosis of genetic generalized epilepsy with typical absence seizures.

He describes recurring daytime absence episodes characterized by brief staring and eyelid fluttering lasting 5 to 10 seconds, occurring approximately once or twice daily. His latest absence spell occurred yesterday, 9 January 2025. He reports no generalized convulsions or myoclonic jerks. He continues sodium valproate 500 mg twice daily.
We agreed to maintain his valproate dose. No EEG requested today. Follow-up in four months.
I evaluated George in clinic today. His diagnosis is genetic generalized epilepsy.

He continues to experience typical absence spells, currently occurring once or twice daily, with the most recent episode noted on 14 May 2025. There have been no convulsive attacks or myoclonic events. He remains on sodium valproate 500 mg twice daily with good reported compliance.
Management plan is unchanged. Routine review in four months.

George was seen for routine review. He has genetic generalized epilepsy on sodium valproate 500 mg twice daily. Absence events continue once or twice daily, latest on 8 September 2025. No convulsions.
